column1: # Provenance of the x86-64 real-project reports (oss-report.py status
# --provenance; the format is in oss-report.py). Hand-kept from the lanes'
# state notes; it says what a report.json does not: the hod commit of a
# frozen copy named by its sha256, and the kiln of a report written before
# reports carried a `kiln` field. Rows of a report that has `kiln` are not
# needed. Update it with the lane when a lane re-freezes hod or kiln.
# hod: frozen copies named by the first 8 hex digits of their sha256
# The hosted real-projects run 44078914310 of exactly a68a0d5d, native on
# GitHub's x86_64 runner (hod a68a0d5d built by the job, binary `hod`; kiln
# 8f93304ee): 14 of its 15 projects are this page's rows (abseil's row is
# the lane's, see its note). Their reports carry no kiln commit; the rows
# below name it for every tree of those not named further down
# frozen copies of the release candidates under other names: the third set's
# copy of cd6ef6bc (WP-211) and the fifth set's copy of e98267c0 (WP-253)
# kiln, first lane set (WP-191): runs 10 to 12 on kiln 1.1.0; abseil's
# -O0 -g strict tree and re2's -O0 trees on kiln 1.2.0 (kiln++ rebuilt in
# place at 01:19Z on 2026-11-15) and re2's on kiln 1.2.0 (run 15)
# kiln 1.2.0 for every tree of the projects first built after the pin move
# (runs 17 and 18; the third set's FlatBuffers), and for every control and
# strict tree of the first set since: the controls rebuilt on kiln 1.2.0
# (ctl-1), the strict re-runs at 02fe2d02, e98267c0 and cd6ef6bc (strict-1,
# strict-2, strict-B/A/C); the hod (hybrid) trees of runs 10 to 12 stay on

column2: Boost (`boost_tmpl`): the hybrid build is the one of hod 56a4695f, which declined 169 objects in each flavour for `asm:section` (module assembly that switches to `.debug_gdb_scripts`; built since WP-255); it was not built again for this page, and the columns `built by hod`, `fell back` and the refusal census below are its. The strict build at a68a0d5d has 631 of 631 offered objects by hod in each flavour and declines none. Every build, the control's included, ends with one of its 528 links failing, hence `failed (0 TUs)`.

Boost (`boost_tmpl`): one of the 528 links fails in every build, the control's included: `multi_index-test_serialization` (undefined `test_serialization2()`, `test_serialization3()` and Boost.Serialization symbols). The lane's Jamfile shim reads only the first line of a multi-line `run` rule and Boost.Serialization is not in the subset; not a compiler difference.
range_v3: one translation unit (`view/tokenize.cpp`) fails to compile upstream in every build, the control's included (clang 19 rejects it too); every object the strict build makes is hod's.

glaze: kiln's front end rejects three translation units in every build, the control's included (`cbor_test.cpp`, `cli_menu_test.cpp`, `msgpack_test.cpp`), and with `-g` the compile of `json_test.cpp` runs out of memory twice in every build as well, hence `failed (3 TUs)` and `failed (5 TUs)`; every object the strict build makes is hod's, and its tests equal the control's test by test.

A test that runs an x86-64 program itself rather than through ctest (a death test re-executing `/proc/self/exe`, a python test script) fails under qemu in the control and in hod's builds alike: the comparison with the control holds, the absolute count does not (googletest's 45 of 63).

scnlib: `scn_stdin_test` is such a test (a python script that starts the x86-64 program itself). It failed in the control and in the hybrid build of 2026-11-15, where the host could not start the program ("rosetta error: failed to open elf at /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2"), and passes in the strict build at a68a0d5d of 2026-11-17: 25 of 25 against 24 of 25. The difference is the host's between the two days, not hod's; why the host starts the program now was not looked into.

mold: mold's ctest list has 1,362 tests on the lane host of 2026-11-17 against 929 on 2026-11-15 (433 `i686-*` tests more: mold adds them when it finds an i686 cross compiler and qemu-i386), so the control was built again on 2026-11-17 at kiln 8f93304ee and the row compares the same 1,362 tests in both trees. Most of them fail in both, the cross-built mold running under qemu-x86_64: 237 pass in the control. `-O0`: equal test by test. `-O0 -g`: one test, `aarch64-sort-debug-info-merged-str`, passes in the strict build and fails in the control; it was not looked into.

zlib (the one stated exception of the lane rows, docs/RELEASE.md section 5): one of 37 objects, `infcover.c`, is compiled with `--coverage`, and kiln never offers such a translation unit to hod (skip reason `coverage`: the gcov instrumentation runs in kiln's LLVM pipeline), so 36 of 37 objects are hod's and the strict build is marked `failed`; the owner's decision of 2026-11-15: not hod's fault, does not block 1.0 (BACKLOG WP-279). `infcover` links in neither build (the linker does not find `libclang_rt.profile.a`, LLVM's profile runtime, on the lane host): 7 of 8 links. Both flavours measured at a68a0d5d against the kiln 8f93304ee controls of WP-278, serial ctest: 5 of 6 tests, the control's. The `-O0 -g` difference seen at e98267c0 is a race in zlib's own tests: `zlib_example` and `zlib_static_example` write the same `foo.gz`; under `ctest -j2` it fails 27 to 36 of 40 runs in the control and in strict alike, serially 0 of 20 (WP-278).
ctre has no ctest tests: its build (the compile-time tests) is the measurement.

fmt, googletest, re2, benchmark, protobuf, spdlog, catch2, nlohmann_json, yaml_cpp, glog, leveldb, cli11, doctest, simdjson (hod cell `a68a0d5d (hosted run 44078914310)`): every tree of these rows (control, hybrid, strict) is from the hosted real-projects run 44078914310 of exactly a68a0d5d: built and tested natively on GitHub's x86_64 runner, hod a68a0d5d built by the job, kiln 8f93304ee. Every other row of this page is cross-built on the AArch64 lane host with its tests run under qemu-x86_64.

abseil: the row is the lane's (cross-built, tests under qemu-x86_64, the strict build at a68a0d5d), where the control and the strict build fail the same one test, `absl_symbolize_test`. The hosted run 44078914310 of a68a0d5d also built and tested abseil natively on an x86_64 runner, both flavours: the control passes 231 of 232 (`absl_raw_hash_set_test` fails), hod's hybrid and strict builds 230 of 232, the same test and `absl_symbolize_test`. That one difference from the control is the listed entry of `docs/status/oss-expected.tsv`: a call to an always_inline function is compiled out of line, so the symbolizer names `inline_func` and not its caller (`spec/cli.md` "Always-inline"). A row is not made of the two hosts' trees together.
